text: When something needs doing and you aren't the one to do it, make a task. It lands on that person's list with everything they need, instead of in a hallway conversation.
Maria Rivera is dropping off a urine sample for Juniper on Friday. Jordan, our tech, needs to run it.
Click plus Task.
The one thing to remember: pick a person when you know who should do it. Leave it unassigned only when anyone on that team can.
To-do is for general work. Callback is for calling a client, and has its own video.
Write what needs doing, short and clear.
Assign it to Jordan Pike.
Queue is only for unassigned work, so leave it on Anyone.
Tick anyone else who should keep an eye on it. Dr. Lane will see it under Watching.
Start today.
Give it a due date. If Friday ends and it isn't done, it moves to Jordan's Expired tab.
Leave it Not Urgent. Urgent jumps to the top of the list, so save it for things that can't wait.
Link the pet, so Juniper's chart is one click away.
Pick Juniper.
Put the details in the notes, not the title.
Tick the office.
Create task.
Here it is, assigned to Jordan, with Dr. Lane watching and the due date set.
Back to list.
Click Sent. Everything you've asked of others is here, so you can check it got done.
The most common mistakes: leaving Assign to blank, so the task sits on a queue nobody watches, and cramming the instructions into the title. Remember: pick a person when you know who should do it.
